name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East for its pine-clad hills, colonial architecture, and cool climate.
facts: Named after U Shillong, a powerful deity
Hub of education in Northeast India

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1965 metres, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills, and sunsets.
facts: About 10 km from Shillong city centre
Popular evening hangout for city lights

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, originally called Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew, set amid lush ferns and rocks.
facts: Named after a rock that resembled an elephant (destroyed in 1897 earthquake)
Easily accessible with stairs between tiers

name: Ward's Lake
description: Historic man-made lake in the heart of Shillong, locally known as Nan Polok, with gravel paths, flower beds, and an arched bridge.
facts: Named after Sir William Ward, Chief Commissioner of Assam
Popular for boating and leisure walks

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum in Shillong showcasing the rich multi-cultural lifestyles and artefacts of indigenous peoples of Northeast India.
facts: One of the finest museums on Northeast indigenous cultures

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic wettest place on Earth on the southern plateau of East Khasi Hills, famous for dramatic waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges.
facts: Once recorded as the wettest place on the planet
Gateway to many natural wonders of the district

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: India's tallest plunge waterfall at 340 metres, cascading from the Cherrapunji plateau into a turquoise pool near Sohra.
facts: Named after the legend of Ka Likai who jumped from the cliff
Fed by rainwater from the small plateau
Best viewed in monsoon for full flow

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented seven-stream waterfall plunging over limestone cliffs near Mawsmai village, one of the most impressive in Meghalaya.
facts: Also known as Seven Sisters Falls or Mawsmai Falls
Dramatic drop over the plateau edge

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra with electric lighting and pathways, offering an easy introduction to Meghalaya's cave systems.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, formed over centuries by guiding Ficus elastica roots, reached by a steep 3500-step trek.
facts: Estimated over 180 years old for the lower level
Only double-decker of its kind in the world

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Asia's cleanest village in Pynursla block, known for spotless streets, bamboo skywalk, living root bridges, and views toward Bangladesh.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003 by Discover India
About 90 km from Shillong near India-Bangladesh border

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic viewpoint translating to 'End of the Hills', offering sweeping vistas of deep valleys, cloud-filled gorges, and rolling ridges near Smit.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove protected by Khasi tradition, where nothing may be removed; rich in biodiversity, monoliths, and old-growth forest.
facts: Rule: take nothing from the forest
Home to ancient trees and Khasi ceremonial sites

name: Kongthong Village
description: Whistling Village where residents use unique maternal tunes (Jingrwai Lawbei) as names, nestled in remote hills between Sohra and Pynursla.
facts: India's entry for UNWTO Best Tourism Villages
About 60 km from Shillong, elevation around 1530 m

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning turquoise waterfall in Amlarem subdivision of West Jaintia Hills, cascading into a natural swimming pool surrounded by limestone cliffs and dense forest. One of Meghalaya's most photogenic and popular falls.
facts: Located near Amlarem, about 30 km from Jowai
Known for clear blue-green water year-round

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megalithic monoliths in Asia, located in Nartiang village. Menhirs and dolmens erected by Jaintia kings and clans between the 16th and 19th centuries to commemorate warriors and ancestors.
facts: Nartiang was summer capital of Jaintia kings

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: 600-year-old Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Durga (Jayanti), one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Believed to be where Sati's left thigh fell; major pilgrimage site especially during Durga Puja.
facts: Located in Nartiang village near the monoliths

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake near Mukhla village on NH-6, also known as Pung Sajar Nangli. According to legend, dug overnight by followers of rebel general Sajar Nangli. Popular for picnics and boating amid pine forests.
facts: Legend of overnight digging by 290 clans

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town and crystal-clear Umngot River famous for glass-like transparent waters where boats appear to float in air. Historic British suspension bridge and Indo-Bangladesh border trade point.

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside adventure village upstream from Dawki on the Umngot River, known for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, snorkeling, and quiet pebble beaches in a scenic gorge.
facts: Popular for riverside camping and water sports
In West Jaintia Hills near India-Bangladesh border

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tiered waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road, cascading over rocks into a valley with views of paddy fields. Accessible via a short walk and arch bridge.
facts: Comparable to Elephant Falls in beauty

name: Jowai Town
description: District headquarters of West Jaintia Hills, cultural and commercial hub of the Pnar people. Gateway to nearby waterfalls, lakes, and monoliths, set on a plateau surrounded by the Myntdu River.
facts: HQ of West Jaintia Hills district
Base for exploring Jaintia Hills attractions

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Hidden double-tiered waterfall near Shkentalang village in West Jaintia Hills, with turquoise pools and a short forest trek. Offbeat gem less crowded than major falls.
facts: Name means paradise in local language
